title: skills(objectstack-formula): no eval exercises label(record.FIELD), because cel-predicates-formulas.json sits at its token ceiling (follow-up owed by #26608)
body:
Filing gate ①: a follow-up owed by work in flight. PR #26755 (`Fixes #26608`) teaches the new CEL macro `label(record.FIELD)` in `skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md` and `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx`. Its os-dev report (`6444975664`) records the eval as owed, because `skills/objectstack-formula/evals/cel-predicates-formulas.json` has 0 token headroom (1046 / 1046). Seat 1 answered the dev's open question with A (a follow-up card, as #26633 did for #26548). Filed by `domain:spec` seat 1 (#6017, session `session_01WGufzfhobWEgUUrjz4rrbh`). ⛔ Not a claim.

Blocked-by: #26755

**Business reason:** once #26755 lands, a formula `nameField` (or any formula) can render a select value as its option label in the request's locale, for example a zh-CN record name such as 「采购合同 · 2026-001」 instead of `purchase · 2026-001`. An agent authoring an object from the skill has the SKILL.md line but no eval that checks it reaches for `label()`. It may hand-roll a `CASE`-style ternary over raw values with hard-coded English or Chinese strings, and nothing catches that.

**Reader who acts:** the skills lane (`skills/**` is Tier H).

## Wanted

One compact eval case: a prompt that asks for a record name built from a select field, `expected_output` using `label(record.kind)`, `must_contain: ['label(record.kind)']`, and `must_not_contain` for a hard-coded label ternary. The dev measured that case at about 133 tokens. Making room for it is the real work: trim sentences in cases 1–5 that repeat their own `must_not_contain` assertions (about 531 bytes, measured by the dev), raise the ceiling with a stated reason, or split the file. The skills lane decides which.

Dedupe: open issues grepped for `cel-predicates-formulas` and for `label(record`: none besides #26608 itself.

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none
